s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital skin disorder with blistering and hyperkeratotic lesions
salient_findings: Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
Bullae and vesicles on the face, trunk, and extremities
key_facts: Normal growth and development for age and sex
Multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae on the face, trunk, and extremities
Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation within the epidermis
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1

raw.syndrome_frame: Congenital skin disorder with blistering and hyperkeratotic lesions
salient_findings: Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
Bullae and vesicles on the face, trunk, and extremities
key_facts: Normal growth and development for age and sex

shortlist.label: Epidermolytic ichthyosis (bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma)
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of hyperkeratotic plaques, erythema, vesicles, and bullae, along with genetic testing revealing a heterozygous variation in KRT1

shortlist.label: Ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical features of hyperkeratotic lesions and blistering, with a possible genetic link to KRT1 or KRT10 mutations

shortlist.label: Bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Matching clinical features of erythema, vesicles, and bullae, with a known association with KRT1 or KRT10 mutations

shortlist.label: Superficial epidermolytic ichthyosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation, although less severe, with a possible link to KRT1 or KRT10 mutations

shortlist.label: Keratinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation in KRT1, which is a key feature of keratinopathies, including epidermolytic ichthyosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple skin lesions, erythema, vesicles, and bullae, along with the skin-punch biopsy revealing hyperkeratosis and bullae formation within the epidermis, and the genetic testing showing a heterozygous variation in KRT1, are all consistent with epidermolytic ichthyosis (bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma).

rejected.label: Ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and genetic findings do not specifically match this condition.

rejected.label: Bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma
rejected.why: This is another term for epidermolytic ichthyosis, but not a distinct diagnosis in this context.

rejected.label: Superficial epidermolytic ichthyosis
rejected.why: The biopsy findings of hyperkeratosis and bullae formation within the epidermis are more characteristic of epidermolytic ichthyosis.

rejected.label: Keratinopathy
rejected.why: While the genetic variation in KRT1 suggests a keratinopathy, the specific clinical and histopathological features point more directly to epidermolytic ichthyosis.
